notes.title: Introducing the Black & Blue Bundle
notes.notes:
We are delighted to introduce the Black and Blue Steam Bundle.

The bundle comprises the inky [b]black[/b] odyssey, Inscryption, by Daniel Mullins Games and the architectural adventure,[b] Blue[/b] Prince, by Dogubomb.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40356052/a7ebb4bcb9a5533f60044d30c13591b49737543b.png[/img]

[h3]About Inscryption[/h3]
Inscryption is a deckbuilding roguelike with escape room style puzzles mixed with some psychological horror from the creator of The Hex and Pony Island.

In Inscryption you will embark on an inky black odyssey and unlock the secrets of Leshy’s cabin with your deck of woodland creature cards.

[h3]Complete the Set[/h3]
The Black and Blue bundle is a “complete the set” bundle, which means that you will pay for and receive just the items you do not already own in your Steam Library at the discounted price.

As fans of Daniel’s work we are excited to be part of this bundle [url=https://x.com/DMullinsGames/status/1771341258218488125]and will always be grateful for his support of Blue Prince.[/url]

Buy the bundle: https://store.steampowered.com/bundle/56346/Black__Blue/

Blue Prince is Out Now

notes.title: Patch 1.05
notes.notes:
[p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40356052/d09c183989ec231d85856d97d2d5fa3031f8e113.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Hello drafters,
[/p][p]We have released patch 1.05 this afternoon for Steam players. This patch addresses a number of issues reported by the community. 

[b]Save Corruption & Loading Freeze Fixes[/b]
[/p][p]We've identified and addressed several edge cases that were causing save file corruption, resulting in a loading freeze when accessing the main menu. Unfortunately, if your save file was affected by these issues, we are sorry to say that means it is corrupted and irretrievable despite our best efforts to find a way to restore it.
[/p][p]This update also includes multiple fixes aimed at preventing these corruption cases from occurring in the future. Several code checks have been added to reduce the chance of corruption including redundant checking of the validity of the save before writing it. Additionally, we’ve implemented an automatic backup system: if the primary save becomes corrupted or lost, a backup save will now load instead.

If you are PS Plus user whose save file has been affected by this, we have had a few encouraging reports from users who were able to restore a backup of their save file via Playstaion Plus cloud storage. To restore from cloud on PS5 follow these steps:
[/p][p]1.	Go to Settings > Saved Data and Game/App Settings.[/p][p]2.	Select Saved Data (PS5).[/p][p]3.	Choose Download or Delete from Cloud Storage.[/p][p]4.	Select the game and then the specific save file you want to restore.[/p][p]5.	Choose Download. 

We are also currently implementing an “IMPORT TROPHY DATA” feature to work with platform achievements that had been previously earned in previous save files (even if they don’t exist in any of your current save files.) This feature will be included in an upcoming patch.

FURTHER CHANGES IN THIS PATCH LISTED BELOW:[/p][list][*][p]Fixed a bug occurring when consecutive Parlor boxes were opened too quickly.[/p][p][/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an input recognition issue on keyboard where \[Right Arrow] and \[A] were incorrectly interpreted as CONFIRM in certain cases.[/p][p][/p][/*][*][p]Corrected some minor magnification issues and inconsistencies in font usage in the following locations - Library, \[spoiler]Master Bedroom\[/spoiler], \[spoiler]Vault. \[/spoiler]
[/p][/*][*][p]Unified all instances of ‘Mary Matthew’ to a consistent spelling. (One instance had a typo.)
[/p][/*][/list][p][b]LATE GAME SPOILERS BELOW[/b][/p][list][*][p]\[spoiler]You can now reset rarity changes that you have made to your floorplans. The method is explained in the Conservatory menu as floorplan rarity can only be reset in the Conservatory).\[/spoiler][/p][p][/p][/*][*][p]\[spoiler]The doors powered by remote power boxes are now opened by button press instead of unlocking automatically. These doors will remain permanently unlocked after being opened.\[/spoiler][/p][p][/p][/*][*][p]\[spoiler]A trunk in the Treasure Trove incorrectly displaying the moon symbol has been changed to the sun symbol. (A blue memo was incorrectly being labeled as false.\[/spoiler][/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p]We also have corrected a few oversights and bugs in the room drafting logic. Below are listed a few of the resulting technical corrections that may be of interest.
[/p][list][*][p]\[spoiler]Master Bedroom will no longer erroneously appear in places other than the East Wing (Rank 9 related bug)\[/spoiler]
[/p][/*][*][p]\[spoiler]Fixed a narrow bug permitting Foundation to be added to the draft pool after repellent use before 7 days had transpired.\[/spoiler][/p][p][/p][/*][*][p]\[spoiler]Foundation will no longer be drawn with as much frequency on Ranks 2 and 3\[/spoiler]
[/p][/*][*][p]\[spoiler]An oversight in outer room drafting logic has been corrected concerning day one and outer room rarities have been slightly flattened across the board.\[/spoiler][/p][/*][/list][p]
The patch is live now on Steam. We expect the patch to be available to Xbox and PlayStation players before the weekend. [/p][p][/p][p]Blue Prince is Out Now[/p][p][/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/1569580/Blue_Prince/"][/dynamiclink][/p][p][/p][p]
[/p]

notes.title: Patch 1.04.5
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40356052/40428a50ea2ab304e5922d255bbe7658168f6d40.jpg[/img]

Hello drafters, 

We have released a patch this afternoon to resolve some issues that the community have been experiencing. The patch is now live on Steam and we expect Xbox and PlayStation players to see this before the weekend. As always, the changelog below includes some spoilers. 

[h1]PlayStation 5 Save Rollback Issue[/h1]
This patch also includes a fix for the PS5 Save Rollback Issue that was preventing players from progressing their explorations of Mount Holly.

This issue was caused by a duplication of save data causing new save information to time out and not be saved. This problem has now been addressed and players should have no issues progressing and saving the game past the point where the bug was initially encountered.

We have worked tirelessly with Sony to avoid any save files being lost once the game patches.However, content that was not saved during the Rollback Issue has unfortunately been lost. Players should be able to return to Mount Holly at the point where they encountered the bug.

[h1]Patch 1.04.5 Changelog:[/h1]
[list]
[*]Fixed the rollback bug that was interfering with saving the game on PlayStation for some users
[*]Fixed a bug occasionally preventing players from entering the highest rank due to a rogue collider.
[*]Fixed a bug that could cause you to lose steps when investigating the east sealed antechamber door while in a gymnasium.
[*]Fixed a potential collider softlock that could occur after [spoiler]digging up treasure in the Cloister.[/spoiler]
[*]Fixed a potential collider softlock that could occur after [spoiler]digging up treasure in the Closet.[/spoiler] 
[*]The experiment [spoiler]“Gain 1 Key, 1 Gem or 1 Gold (selected at random)” has been changed to “Gain 1 Key, 1 Gem, or 1 Die (selected at random)”[/spoiler]
[*]Unified all instances of "Christoph" to a consistent spelling.
[*]Typo fixed in Glossary entry for “Directory”.
[/list]

[h1]LATE GAME SPOILER CHANGELOG BELOW - Read at own risk[/h1]
[list]
[*][spoiler]Boat Ride cinematics can now be once again skipped (this had been disabled because of a soft lock that has also now been fixed.)[/spoiler]
[*][spoiler]Lever pull cinematics can now be skipped.[/spoiler]
[*][spoiler]Added additional safety checks to address reported soft locks some users reported encountering in the Casino.[/spoiler]
[*][spoiler]The 7-letter title in the Gallery now accepts an overlooked regional spelling as a valid solution[/spoiler]
[*][spoiler]Boudoir Safe now accepts one alternate regional solution.[/spoiler]
[*][spoiler]Safes now remain open on subsequent days after unlocking them.[/spoiler]
[*][spoiler]A bug has been fixed in Maid’s Chamber and Servant’s Quarter that would occasionally cause payroll to not spawn.[/spoiler]
[*][spoiler]A bug has been fixed in an upgraded guest bedroom that was causing a one-time trigger to occur multiple times.[/spoiler]
[/list]

[h1]EVEN DEEPER SPOILER CHANGELOG BELOW[/h1]
[list]
[*][spoiler]Edited the wording of “Question 33” to provide more clarity. The solution remains unchanged.[/spoiler]
[*][spoiler]Cleaned up the mathematical symbols of “Question 46” to provide more clarity. The solution remains unchanged.[/spoiler]
[*][spoiler]Unified Date formatting in terminal logs for consistency.[/spoiler]
[*][spoiler]Repositioned a (Blue Tents) memo in a ‘found floorplan’ to fix a bug causing it to occasionally not appear. (no content change)[/spoiler]
[*][spoiler]The experiment that “lowers water” will now be replaced with an experiment variation that “raises water” if there is not currently any water to lower.[/spoiler]
[*][spoiler]The experiment “Each time you view your map, lose 10 steps and then” has been changed to “The next 10 times you view your map, lose 10 steps and then”[/spoiler]
[*][spoiler]The experiment “Gain 1 Key for every 40 steps you have” has been changed to “Gain 1 Key for every 30 steps you have”[/spoiler]
[*][spoiler]The experiment “Gain 1 Key, 1 Gem or 1 Gold (selected at random)” has been changed to “Gain 1 Key, 1 Gem, or 1 Die (selected at random)”[/spoiler]
[*][spoiler]On Day One, the trunk in the bedroom will no longer only appear after the first draft.[/spoiler]
[/list]

[spoiler]We would also like to add that we are currently working on a feature to use the Blackbridge Terminal’s “IMPORT TROPHY DATA” feature to work with platform achievements that have been previously earned (even if they don’t exist in any of your current save files.) We expect this feature to be completed soon and will be included in an upcoming patch, thank you for your patience.[/spoiler]

[h1]The Path to 1.10[/h1]

It had always been my dream to release a definitive version of the game at launch. I’m a big fan of complete standalone experiences and it was never my plan to continually tinker with the game with regular content updates, room rebalancing, or DLC and the like. Considering this is my first game, I’m extremely proud of everything I managed to include for launch, but there are a few minor things that were not quite completed before our release date that I feel must be added to fulfill that original vision

Those inclusions will be added in [b]1.10[/b], which will be the final major update to the game. It will be the definitive version of the game. 

Among the planned inclusions in this final update: an overhyped arcade game, a curious house cat, accessibility features like color assist mode, controls remapping, cursor size/opacity settings, and widescreen support. Some UI/UX improvements, more variations for end-of-day manor descriptions and accompanying house illustrations, HUD display customization, final room/item balancing, and the addition of a handful of extra cinematics that I am still working on (the unlockable challenge modes actually have their own unique openings and endings!)


NOTE: We will continue to release bug-fixing patches intermittently in the months leading up to 1.10 and some of these updates may preemptively roll out some of the above-mentioned features (we wouldn’t want to sit on accessibility features for months on end while we wait on cinematics!) And while 1.10 will be the last planned content update, we will, of course, continually be committed to fixing bugs for far, far into the future.

[i] - Tonda Ros, Director of Blue Prince[/i]

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1569580/Blue_Prince/

We have released a patch this afternoon to address some issues that players reported experiencing. The changelog below includes spoilers.
[list]
[*]Expanded video playback compatibility for even more Steam Deck configurations!

If you are impacted by this issue please submit a ticket to our support desk: https://rawfury.atlassian.net/servicedesk/customer/portal/1 including your PSN ID and the size of your save file to help the team narrow in on a fix.

We thank you for your patience while we work on this issue.

As soon as we have an update about the PS5 save rollback issue we will make an announcement to let everyone know.

notes.title: Day One at Mount Holly
notes.notes:
Hello drafters,

The first 24 hours of sharing Blue Prince with you all has been incredible. Thank you for your support of the game. After 8 years in development it’s wonderful to see people walking the halls, exploring the rooms and uncovering the secrets that Mount Holly holds.

notes.title: Blue Prince (PC) Review
notes.notes:
Blue Prince is a puzzle game shrouded with mystery, featuring over 40+ craftable floorplans, many permanent upgrades to improve your runs onward, and reaching the mysterious 46th room to claim your inheritance to the manor.

Developed by Dougbomb and published by Raw Fury, Blue Prince is a charming puzzle game incorporating RNG and roguelike elements. When I started the game, I felt a Resident Evil vibe. But instead of solving puzzles in Spencer Mansion filled with zombies, you are solving puzzles from the rooms you crafted, learning about the family history that is shrouded with mysteries regarding an unsolved case, and finding access to the mysterious 46th room to claim your inheritance to the manor.

Stepping into the manor, you are greeted by a letter from your uncle explaining that the manor is your inheritance—but only if you can reach the 46th room. To achieve this goal, the letter outlines that players cannot stay overnight or use objects outside the manor... Read more

notes.title: Dev Blog #3 - Watch Your Steps
notes.notes:
In the last [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1569580/view/4196868529807943357]dev blog[/url] we explored the estate of Mount Holly, the mysterious manor where you will spend your time in Blue Prince, examining every room and rumor, day by day…

…and [b]step[/b] by [b]step[/b].

You see, there’s only so much one can do in a single day. Scouring a gigantic estate for clues, after all, can be a very exhausting task.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40356052/e6895df565ad0e3dbdbbc02679f724136808c98f.png[/img]

In Blue Prince, [b]STEPS[/b] represent how much energy you have. You will start every morning with 50 steps, and you will find that number in the top left corner of the screen. But there’s no need to rush! Steps are only lost when moving between rooms. So, you can take your time and spend as much time as you like in each room to explore (and we encourage that!).

And hey, 50 steps to find the 46th room of the house seems perfectly reasonable, right?

[i]Right…?[/i]

Well, let’s just say that you can’t always line up rooms in a straight path to where you are aiming to go. Drafting your house will involve a lot of strategic architectural weaving, unexpected turns, and nasty dead-ends that always seem to pop up at the most inopportune times! If you’re not careful, those steps are going to quickly be depleted as you trek around looking for doors that you passed up earlier in the day. Once you run out of steps, you will have to [i][b]Call it a Day[/b][/i].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40356052/f7caf54e075945b39eced8b9be0e6fbe452aa4c9.png[/img]

But all hope is not lost! There are several ways to increase your steps whilst inside the manor. Fruit found around the house will give you a quick boost of energy, replenishing a handful of steps, and there are even rooms that you can rest up in to gain even more! One such example is [b]BEDROOM[/b], which will give you [b]+2 STEPS[/b] each time that you enter the room. Quite useful if you draft it in a spot in your house that you plan on traveling through again later.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40356052/b5bbe95e167d5b4fed9fe103b340397f5f3ce72b.png[/img]

If you’re the type of player who loves to explore and wander off the path to investigate and look for secrets, then you may be in need of even more steps than the occasional fruit or bedroom can provide. A room like [b]NURSERY[/b] has the potential to provide a massive amount of steps. That is, if you draft more bedrooms. It is also worth noting that [b]NURSERY[/b] is a dead-end. So if you draft this room in your house you may not have as many options for expansion.

Tough choices lie ahead. You are the architect of your journey to Room 46, choose wisely!

Blue Prince is coming to Steam soon, wishlist now! https://store.steampowered.com/app/1569580/Blue_Prince/

Join us on [url=https://discord.com/invite/BluePrince]Discord[/url]
Follow us on [url=https://x.com/dogubomb]Twitter[/url]

notes.title: Dev Blog #2 - Mount Holly Estate
notes.notes:
[h2][b]Living Wills and Dead Ends[/b][/h2]

Mount Holly, ‘the House of Shifting Rooms’ (as the locals call it), is a sprawling estate resting in the saddle of the Reddington Mountains directly south of the tree line. Once the esteemed domain of your great uncle, Mount Holly now falls under your ownership. Yet an intriguing condition accompanies the inheritance: you must locate the hidden 46th Room of this mysterious 45-room estate.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40356052/1a555432b307102697ead91ffe285e05ff192cec.png[/img]

One of the most interesting features of this unique house is the way the rooms work. In Mount Holly, opening a door does not always lead to the same room. Floorplans shift, things move around and each day the entire blueprint of the house changes. One day you may find a kitchen leading off from the Entrance Hall, the next, a gymnasium. You really can’t take anything for granted.

The central mechanic of Blue Prince is a process that will at once be familiar to both architects and card players called [b]DRAFTING[/b]. When you open a door on the estate, you will be given three potential room options to choose between. As the architect, [i]you[/i] decide from those selections which floorplan you want to build. Each door in Mount Holly is a choice, and the choices you make will shape your adventure.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40356052/1b3c25d87dfc4099e2e70faf45cdf2b69536089c.jpg[/img]

Mount Holly provides a wide variety of rooms for you to choose from that range from commonplace to rare. From this pool of rooms, you will progress each day, drafting one room at a time, expanding and exploring the house and its many mysteries as you progress. When you can no longer make progress, for example, if you can’t find any new doors to open, you may [b]‘Call it a Day’[/b] to reset your house and start fresh the next morning with a brand new blueprint.

Mount Holly is an architectural conundrum and there’s so much more about the house we could expand on but I think it’s best if we leave the majority of its many mysterious doors closed… for now.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40356052/f4fbf6485edf89e5fbc09cf0e1c55dba4b3b2f98.png[/img]

We’re really excited for people to soon be able to get hands on with the game, if you’re as hyped as we are we have a [url=https://www.discord.gg/blueprince]Discord[/url] server for all things Blue Prince, join us.

notes.title: Dev Blog #1 - The Drafting of Blue Prince
notes.notes:
[b][h2]Welcome to Mount Holly[/h2][/b]

Are your bags packed yet? Are you ready to begin your search for Room 46? You play as Simon, who has inherited the title and deed to Mount Holly, a puzzling mansion on a sprawling estate. But the inheritance you have received comes with a catch…

[previewyoutube=2cEKyYhC-Eg;full][/previewyoutube]

The debut game of Tonda Ros, a visual artist and independent game developer based out of Hollywood. After a decade of working in the film industry and making stuff for other people, Tonda finally decided in 2016 to make something for himself. The following eight years can only be described as a labour of love.

[i]“This was a project that I initially had expected to be finished in six months. But what’s a year or eight more among friends? I stopped keeping track a while ago.” [/i]- Tonda

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40356052/f21fd7726bdff65239a5208333295cfcd140baea.png[/img]

We sat down with Tonda from Dogubomb to talk about how Blue Prince came to be.

[h3][b]The Idea of Blue Prince[/b][/h3]

[b]Q: When did you come up with the initial idea for Blue Prince?[/b]

A: I had been tinkering for years with a few board game ideas and different design elements that eventually wound up together in the game, but the spring of 2016 was when all these disparate ideas came together under the umbrella of a video game concept.

[b]Q: How did this concept come about?[/b]

A: When I first started learning Unity, my only intention was to casually explore the technology and gauge how difficult it would be to make a game. On my second day in the program, I started working on a first-person test scene because without a character I didn’t need to figure out character animation to get my feet wet. I love first-person games and exploration so I started copy-pasting rooms and made a really big house with a lot of doors. Nothing is more fun to me than being in a room with multiple doors and having to pick one to investigate. That fundamental idea was the core concept I wanted to explore. Choosing between doors and choosing between rooms. I named that first test scene “House of One Hundred Doors”. That was Day Two. It would be another two years before that project was renamed to “Blue Prince”.

[b]Q: Was it always the plan to make the game a mystery strategy game?[/b]

A: I feel like if you let ten people play Blue Prince and then asked them what genre they’d classify the game, you’d get ten different answers. I didn’t try to fit this thing into a box and I’ve noticed players tend to focus on different aspects of the game that appeal to them, which in turn changes their perspective on the game's categorization.

[b]Q: Was this game based on a love of other games like this?[/b]

A: Actually, the game’s inspirational sources are mainly books and board games, but there’s no one wellspring that I heavily drew from. “Blue Prince” is more of a blended combination of a lot of things I love from a lot of different mediums. Speaking as a player, I’m not a big fan of derivative work in games. To me, there’s an extremely fine line between inspiration and imitation. I try my best to stay pretty far away from that line. But over eight years of development, I’m sure I skirted it a few times.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40356052/a43c8638e5e5bcd3ade50403e6f7812f1db0b37b.png[/img]

[h3][b]Making Blue Prince[/b][/h3]

[b]Q: When did development of the game officially start?[/b]

A: At some point during the first three months that original test scene stopped being a test. It evolved and I didn’t have the heart to press B to stop it. Perhaps it was the day I created the first design document and laid out the drafting mechanic. Perhaps it was the day I first let a friend play a build and saw the look of disbelief on their face. Or maybe it was the day I quit “my job” to focus on the game full time. It was sometime in 2016.

[b]Q: Was this with the same team as Dogubomb has now?[/b]

A: I was working completely solo for the first two years. So no, the Blue Prince team was formed very slowly, piece by piece over the course of the project and the roster has changed many times over.

[b]Q: What were the main challenges in making the game?[/b]

A: By far, the biggest hurdle was maintaining mental stamina throughout such a long, long project. I worked about 80 hours a week on average, which I think is only sustainable if you really love what you are doing and don’t really know how much longer it’s going to take! Throughout development, I always believed the game was one year away from being complete. It’s easy to run in the desert when you see water. It doesn’t matter how dehydrated or tired you are. If you see water, you’re up and running. That’s what it was like. The game’s finish line was an ever-motivating, ever-moving goalpost that was always just out of reach, like a mirage on the desert horizon.

[b]Q: What were some of your favourite parts of the development process?[/b]

A: This one’s really easy to answer. Without a doubt my favorite thing in the process has been watching playtesters play the game. It's hard to imagine a game developer answering anything else honestly. The amount of joy I get from watching people play is ridiculous. I felt the same way at GDC watching people finally getting to experience the game.I think it helps that everyone’s playthrough is so unique. I’m constantly being surprised by things players are coming up with and the individual way they each approach the challenges of the game. It really never gets old.

[b]Q: How are you feeling about the fact the game will launch soon?[/b]

A: Thirsty!

notes.title: Welcome to Mt. Holly
notes.notes:
Welcome Drafters,  

We were delighted to see the trailer for Blue Prince shown at the Future Game Show this evening. If you missed it, you can check it out here:  

[previewyoutube=2cEKyYhC-Eg;full][/previewyoutube]

[h1]What is Blue Prince? [/h1]
Blue Prince is a genre-defying mystery strategy puzzle adventure unlike anything you’ve ever played before.  

You play as Simon, the sole beneficiary of the Sinclair Estate at Mount Holly, a sprawling 45-room Manor set in beautiful and expansive grounds. Your grand-uncle: Herbert S Sinclair, recently passed away and you travel to Mount Holly to claim your inheritance. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40356052/b90b333febe8b0a863833a87d95b7668ec2dd35e.jpg[/img]

But it’s not going to be that simple… 

Herbert was a mysterious and enigmatic man when he was alive, and he has left his biggest challenge yet for you to solve: Find the hidden Room 46 in the 45-room Estate.  

Mount Holly’s shifting nature means that traversing through its halls is an unpredictable journey where no two days play out the same. You also cannot take for granted what room awaits behind any door, floorplans change daily, and every day you start completely from scratch. 

Can you solve the mystery of Mount Holly and find what awaits within Room 46? 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40356052/1b3c25d87dfc4099e2e70faf45cdf2b69536089c.jpg[/img]

[h2]A note from the developer [/h2]
[i]“We’re thrilled to finally have Blue Prince formally introduced to the world. This has been a journey (and house) 8 years in the making, and we can’t wait to unlock the doors of Mount Holly soon and welcome you into our world.”  - [b]Tonda, Director of Blue Prince[/b] [/i]

Blue Prince is coming to Steam soon, follow the game and wishlist now!
